classification.text_en: The sun is a creation of God, one of the sun, the moon and the stars subjected by His command, and one of His signs. People are told not to prostrate to it but to God who made it.

origin.text_en: God made the sun together with the night, the day and the moon, and made it a lamp (siraj) in the heavens.

purpose.text_en: The sun is made a radiance and the moon a light, with the moon set in stations, so that people know the number of years and the reckoning. God did not create this except with truth.

nature.text_en: The sun is called a lamp, a blazing lamp (siraj wahhaj) and a source of radiance (diya'), while the moon is called a light (nur).

abilities.text_en: The sun runs to a settled place (mustaqarr) set for it; the verse does not explain whether that is a place or a term. It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each moves along in its own course (falak).

limitations.text_en: The sun moves by God's command and cannot overtake the moon. It is not to be worshipped. On the Last Day it will be wrapped up, and the sun and the moon will be joined together.

relationship_with_humans.text_en: The sun and the moon are subjected to people, constantly following their course. The people of Saba are described as prostrating to the sun instead of God, and Satan made their deeds look good to them.

quranic_events.text_en: Ibrahim saw the sun rising and said this was his lord; when it set, he told his people he had nothing to do with what they associated with God. Yusuf saw in a dream eleven stars, the sun and the moon bowing to him. Dhul-Qarnayn reached the setting-place of the sun.

chronological_position.note_en: The Quran does not say on which of the six days the sun was made.

location.text_en: In the heavens, set among the constellations: God made in the sky constellations and a lamp and a luminous moon.

misconceptions.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The sun 'running' is the verse's wording. This profile does not read it as a statement about which body moves around which, and leaves any comparison with modern astronomy to the separate Quran & Science module.

lessons.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The sun is presented as a sign to give thanks to God for, never as something to bow to. Its regularity is used to point to the One who decreed it.

vocabulary.text_en: Shams is the sun; siraj is a lamp; wahhaj means blazing; diya' is radiance; mustaqarr is a settled place; falak is a course in which the sun, the moon, the night and the day move; kuwwirat means wrapped up.
